items.note: S1.3 states the three-stage exchange restoring arbitrary scratch values, and its quote gives y_S -> y_S + x_S. It calls the result an exchange without the sign (X,Y) -> (-Y,X) of the complex construction and omits the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule and the net-change argument (JV+RG)x.

S1.4 correctly says that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so endpoint frames fix the operator and edges only change frames. It never writes the edge operator D_v D_u^{-1}, the identity D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, or the per-route form eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}.

S1.5.1 states nested nondegenerate labels, central returns as the only decreasing edges, sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L and L<N/2. It omits L=Ich, the loss h per edge and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The S1.5 method sketches the labels but not the residual table or the telescoping at gates.

S1.5.2 states the permutation rho, endpoint difference I_m on every role and s<Wm, but not the value s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b, and it describes all terminal matrices as projections. The S1.5 method (rank of projection difference = dimension change) follows the paper but misses the essential source exception: -P_{U_a} at X_a gives a rank-one edge 2P_{U_a}, which turns -2N into -N.

S2.1 states that the phase frames C_U turn each edge into translation kernels aI+bX_v. It does not say there is one kernel per orthonormal residual vector, nor give s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c < W_c m, nor say that diagonal corrections give C^{tensor m} on every role. S2.3 only cites s_c as a child count.

The plan states s<Wm for the bit network, L<N/2 and s/W<m^tau with tau<1. It never states s_c<W_c m, the deficits eta_b and eta_c, or the value tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, which appears only implicitly through g_2=2^{-181} in S6.1.

S1.1 and S1.2 state the O(V) elementary stream operations and the controlled shift/unit multiplication. The fiber split-and-swap idea in S1.2 matches the proof at 575-581. The offset-preparation condition b^{O(1)} appears only in the quote.

The statements match Lemmas lem:lower-lower and lem:matrix-shear, and the route (factor, triangular parts as controlled shifts, one interchange per one of Pi) is the paper's. Missing: the three-operation trick D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j that realizes H_i+=D_j with one interchange, the choice of the prime q, and the elimination proof of the factorization.

S1.7 gives the recurrence F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with s calls on volume V/W and the O(e^tau) solution. The S1 method gives the route (network shear, edges by smaller interchanges). Missing: the row field divisible by W^k, the cyclic row split into W role streams, the conversion of the shear into an interchange (D-=H, H+=D, D=H-D), and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule that keeps the node overhead at O(V).

S1 and S1.8 state the O(Vu^tau) bound for arbitrary equal widths and mention extra rows and base-m pieces. They do not show that the rows come from the chunks' own top rho digits or that binary ranges are padded to [q^e], and the phrase 'padding to power widths' misdescribes the decomposition (see errors).

The plan gives H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D, the reduction of e axes to s_c children on e/m axes, and 'binary basis changes by packed additions'. It omits the conjugation by P_M that puts residual directions on coordinate slots, and the formula that makes an inverse child one forward call, (C^{-1})^{tensor f} = (-i)^f Z C Z.

The route matches the paper: eight conditional additions, a guard-defined bad set B with |B| <= delta_bad M, agreement off B, and repair by sorting only the exceptional records. delta_bad = min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}} and the full time bound are not given. The bijection argument that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B, the separate handling of the top selected position and the use for an F_2 change of basis are not shown.

S2.3 gives s_c children on e/m axes, each with 1/W_c of the volume, and S2.4 cites 'the row construction and the recurrence' with result O(Vd^{lambda'}). The recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the leaf cutoff e<d^beta, the row index from the first q_0 chunks and the condition on lambda' are absent.

S2 and S2.4 state O(Vd^{lambda'}) with lambda'<1, exact intermediate values and one truncation with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, without the parameter hypotheses (K = floor(d^c), the bands for d and r). The route (C layer by the phase network, packed basis changes, recurrence, back to H_0) is the paper's. The guard-width bound Delta = ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p) that makes exact evaluation affordable is missing.

The steps state omega_t = y^{2r/t}, F^+F^- = I/t, bit-reversed B_t F_t^- consumed by F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, the layout L and the cost formula. The error bound sqrt2 l 2^{-p} and the exact counterparts L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} of the whole transform are not given, and the layout construction is not shown.
S3.4 gives evaluation at 2^{4p}, the established multiplier, signed extraction and O(rp log(rp)). It does not say that the lemma returns Q_p(fg/r) with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}.

The statement (normalized (f*g)/T, error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, cost) and the route (retain the LB order because the pointwise product commutes with record permutations) match the paper. Missing: the normalization identity F^-(f*g) = M F^-f F^-g, the final exact scaling by M, and the error propagation.

The one-dimensional identity with its hypotheses, error and cost, and the tensor identity RF_s = 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A, are stated. gamma = 2d alpha^2, the definitions of P_s and P_t, and the axis-exposure cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)) are missing, and the S4 method does not show the one-dimensional proof.

Both identities are stated: the chirp form of Q F_t and (RF^+_s)[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)] = u*v/S^2. The chirp a_j = exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) is never defined, and the plan does not say that RF^+_s is obtained by conjugation.

Sizes, prime intervals, alpha, alpha^4 theta_i > p and T/2<S<T follow the paper's order. The fixed exponent values and eta = 1/(4d) are not stated. The existence of the primes (the HvdH/Rosser-Schoenfeld count and the disjointness of the intervals) is only asserted.

The map Phi with mu_i = P_i^{-1} mod s_i, the convolution-preserving isomorphism, the triangular formula, the prefix-controlled shifts and the cost match the paper. The order-S argument for bijectivity and the axis reordering by chunk swaps, the source of the l^tau factor, are not shown.

S5.4 states the twist by e^{pi i k/r} into C[y]/(y^r+1) and the correct wrap after untwisting, which is the paper's construction. The composite M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T is not written out.

The source transform (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma, exact counterpart RF_s) and the six-step algorithm are given, with the two factors S explained. The input digit scaling by 2^{-b-2} and the definition of the opposite transform by conjugation are missing, and S5.6 misstates the second scale (see errors).

The error chain 5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s = 9 2^gamma TL, E_w < 28 2^gamma T^2 L, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, rounding and carries below 2^{2b} all match the paper's route. The disk margins are summarized rather than detailed.

Margins g_1..g_7, min = 2^{-181} = 2 kappa, setup o(V), absorption of log factors and the schoolbook cutoff all match. The seven normalized costs (dK, pK^{tau-1}, l d^{lambda'}, d^2(1+l^tau), d p^{1/2+delta} alpha, d p^delta, log(rp)) are not tabulated against their margins, and the o(V) bound on exceptional-record sorting across calls is not mentioned.
S0 says the bound refutes the n log n conjecture in this model but gives no formulation: no eventual lower bound c_A n lg n and no liminf argument.

errors.says: Rational projection matrices at gates and terminals give endpoint difference I_m on every role (and, via the S1.5 method, ranks equal dimension changes).
errors.paper: Sources X_a get the negative projection -P_{U_a}, not a projection; it is essential to the endpoint identity, and its first edge 2P_{U_a} has rank one where the dimension change is zero, so s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b rather than the dimension sum W m - 2N + 2L.

errors.says: Padding to power widths and enough rows, and handling the remaining widths in base m, extends the interchange.
errors.paper: Widths are not padded to powers of m. The width is split into base-m pieces, each handled by the power-width procedure. Rows come from the chunks' own top rho digits, padded to a multiple of W^k, and binary ranges are padded to [q^e].

errors.says: Each shift is a chunk interchange costing O(VL^tau).
errors.paper: Each rotation is a controlled cyclic shift costing O(V) (Lemma lem:ordered-affine-streams). The O(VL^tau) chunk swaps (at most sixteen) only move the target chunk into position and back.

errors.says: The algorithm applies ... the two rescalings by S and 2^{2b+4} ...
errors.paper: The first rescaling is by S and the second by 2^{2b+4}S, so S occurs twice, as the step's own final clause and S5.7.4 imply.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: interchange by the bit network, the butterfly layer by the complex network, synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling with the chirp and permutation cancellation, the CRT/twist assembly, exact recovery, and the margin table giving kappa = 2^{-181}/2. It thins out in the finite-network core. The label budget, the rank saving and both interfaces are stated rather than derived: the -P_{U_a} source correction behind s_b, s_c<W_c m, the explicit tau = 1-2^{-50} and the layer recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) are missing. It also omits the guard-width bound that makes the exact layer affordable.
